articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors for 2026 Edition
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach has announced 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 edition, taking place December 4-6.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach has announced its exhibitor lineup and reconfigured showfloor for the 2026 edition, bringing together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP previews on December 2 and 3, the fair features a redesigned layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The new floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less space, creating a more focused environment where major galleries are distributed across the venue to improve navigation and sightlines. The fair is organized across sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, alongside the digital art initiative Zero 10. Latin America and the Caribbean maintain a robust presence, with Brazil representing the third-largest national contingent. Alongside the main exhibition floors, the public will be able to view outdoor presentations, including a new body of work by James Turrell and a participatory exhibition in Collins Park brought by the Public Art Fund.

articles.originalTitle: The 90s: Art and Fashion - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Britain Explores Art and Fashion of the 1990s
articles.excerpt: A Tate Britain exhibition explores the creative energy of the 1990s by bringing together photography, fashion, art, and design.
articles.content: Tate Britain presents an exhibition examining the cultural transformation of the 1990s, drawing on the experience of curator Edward Enninful. The presentation unites works by artists and photographers such as Steve McQueen, Sarah Lucas, Yinka Shonibare, Corinne Day, and Juergen Teller, alongside fashion designs by Vivienne Westwood, Alexander McQueen, and John Galliano. Visitors can encounter works that examine a period when boundaries between art, fashion, and popular culture shifted. Featured pieces include Mark Leckey's video work tracing British dance music culture, a tartan look from Vivienne Westwood's Anglomania collection inspired by 18th-century French aesthetics, and Yinka Shonibare's sculpture connecting imperial wealth to historical textile routes. The exhibition also includes Steve McQueen's silent film Bear, Abigail Lane's wall installation, and Jim Lambie's psychedelic floor design Zobop constructed from colored vinyl tape. The exhibition runs at Tate Britain from 8 October 2026 to 14 February 2027, with free admission available for museum members.

articles.originalTitle: New Museum Announces 36 Artists and Collectives for 2027 Triennial - ARTnews.com
articles.title: New Museum Announces 36 Artists and Collectives for 2027 Triennial
articles.excerpt: New York's New Museum has announced the 36 artists and collectives selected for the sixth Triennial, running from February 4 to May 16, 2027.
articles.content: New York's New Museum has announced the 36 artists and collectives participating in the 2027 Triennial, titled "The Outside Expands." Scheduled to run from February 4 to May 16, 2027, the sixth edition of the Triennial marks the first to take place at the museum following its recent expansion. According to the museum, this iteration is the first to be curated by an international team and features the widest international representation in the event's history, with participants hailing from 34 countries. The artist roster includes closely watched figures such as Virginia Chihota, Mandy El-Sayegh, Jesús Hilario-Reyes, Josi, Jota Mombaça, Agnes Questionmark, and Sin Wai Kin. The exhibition takes partial inspiration from a 1979 artist intervention by the collective 3NÓS3 under Brazil's dictatorship, which encouraged cultural workers to look beyond institutional boundaries. The upcoming exhibition highlights artists who destabilize fixed notions of territory, identity, gender, and sexuality while fostering alternate ways of forming collaborations and kinships.

articles.originalTitle: Bilbao Fine Arts Museum gains new €45m Norman Foster-designed wing - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Bilbao Fine Arts Museum Opens New Norman Foster-Designed Wing
articles.excerpt: The Fine Arts Museum in Bilbao, Spain, has opened its new €45m wing designed by architects Norman Foster and Luis María Uriarte. Described as a floating pavilion, the expansion doubles the museum's exhibition space.
articles.content: Located in the industrial port city of Bilbao in Spain's Basque Country, the Fine Arts Museum has opened its new €45m expansion designed by Foster + Partners in collaboration with Luis María Uriarte. Described as a floating pavilion, the striking project doubles the museum's exhibition space to approximately 6,000 sq. m and remodels 8,000 sq. m of existing galleries. The extension connects a 1945 Neo-Classical building and a 1970 Modernist structure, sitting above them with two curved upper storeys held up by giant V-shaped supports. The uppermost floor houses temporary exhibitions, a viewing terrace, a restaurant, and dedicated spaces for architecture and design. Funding for the project came from the Basque government, the regional government, the provincial council, Bilbao city council, and the privately-owned BBK Banking Foundation. Museum director Miguel Zugaza noted that the design respects existing architecture while integrating previous styles. Situated roughly 500 metres from the Guggenheim Museum, the Fine Arts Museum aims to expand its cultural offering as the Basque Country's national gallery.

articles.originalTitle: Cosima von Bonin’s soft toys storm the Petit Palais - Art Basel
articles.title: Cosima von Bonin’s Textile Sculptures to Feature at Petit Palais
articles.excerpt: German artist Cosima von Bonin will present her oversized fabric sculptures at the Petit Palais for Art Basel Paris's public program in the exhibition Dollys & Beaux.
articles.content: Kenyan-born German artist Cosima von Bonin is preparing to open her exhibition titled Dollys & Beaux at the Petit Palais as part of the Art Basel Paris public program. The exhibition brings together the artist's oversized textile sculptures crafted from velvet, leather, and mohair, which initially appeared during Loewe's Fall/Winter 2026 fashion show. Figures such as a midnight-blue velvet St. Bernard dog, sea scallops, a killer whale, and a hermit crab challenge institutional seriousness through humor and absurdity. Spanning a career of over four decades, von Bonin's practice maintains a hands-off approach that prioritizes complete interpretive freedom for the audience. Rarely providing public commentary on her own intentions, the artist uses her work to present a subtle resistance against cultures driven by relentless productivity and speed. Having achieved international recognition through numerous prior exhibitions since her Cologne days, von Bonin continues to question the notion that art must remain solemn to hold significance. The presentations will run from October 23 to 25, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: The 13 Exhibitions to See in October 2026 - ArtReview
articles.title: Essential Art Exhibitions to See Around the World in October 2026
articles.excerpt: Notable art exhibitions opening in October 2026 across global hubs like London, Paris, Tokyo, and Tunis feature works and retrospectives by Brook Hsu, Christoph Schlingensief, and other artists.
articles.content: Among the prominent global art exhibitions for October 2026, London's Heidi gallery hosts Brook Hsu's first UK solo exhibition, which draws inspiration from Richard Brautigan's novella and reinterprets Gustave Courbet's Trout motifs. In Berlin, Gropius Bau stages a large retrospective dedicated to Christoph Schlingensief, featuring restaged environments, videos, and documents from his career as a dramaturg and activist. In the greater Paris area, the newly established 5,000-square-meter art space Large opens on the site of a former Renault factory with the Imaginary Motors exhibition, created in partnership with the automaker's arts foundation. At Edouard Montassut, Phung-Tien Phan presents assemblages exploring commercial interests and identity archetypes. Yokohama Civic Art Gallery Azamino mounts Suburban Interference, featuring approximately seven artist groups focusing on urban space and street culture. Finally, MAM Rio displays Andréa Hygino's sculptural installation integrating school chairs into playground structures to highlight constraints within educational environments.

articles.originalTitle: How an EU-funded research programme has been future-proofing art conservation - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: EU-Funded GoGreen Research Programme Explores Sustainable Art Conservation Methods
articles.excerpt: Involving 13 European institutions and backed by a €3.27m grant, the GoGreen research programme aims to develop sustainable and non-toxic methods for cultural heritage conservation.
articles.content: As museums address their environmental impact, conservators are seeking ways to ensure preservation does not compromise the future. Funded with a €3.27m grant through the EU's Horizon Europe programme, the four-year GoGreen project brought together experts from 13 European institutions. Concluding in September, the programme sought to align conservation with the European Green Deal's 2050 climate neutrality objectives. To treat a 1906 silver Tiffany dish, the Rijksmuseum adopted an L-cysteine solution developed by Qing Wu at Haute École Arc Conservation-restauration in Switzerland, replacing aggressive chemical dips or abrasive chalk. Conservators noted that the cysteine method is safer for humans, the environment, and the object, while allowing better control over surface tarnish. Coordinated by the University of Amsterdam, the project explored energy-efficient climate control and greener cleaning practices across eight work packages. Participating institutions shared their findings through academic publications, lectures, and workshops to guide future conservation approaches.

articles.originalTitle: On World Architecture Day 2026: A Call to Build Better, Build Differently, and Share Resources - ArchDaily
articles.title: International Union of Architects Issues Call on World Architecture Day Addressing Housing Crisis
articles.excerpt: The International Union of Architects marked World Architecture Day by highlighting the global housing crisis, calling on architects to advance equitable housing access through design, research, and advocacy.
articles.content: The International Union of Architects marked World Architecture Day in alignment with United Nations World Habitat Day to draw attention to the global housing crisis. The organization notes that the crisis encompasses multiple barriers to accessing adequate living spaces rather than just a shortage of buildings. According to United Nations figures, more than 3 billion people lack adequate housing, while over 1.1 billion reside in informal settlements. Addressing this multidimensional problem requires building better, sharing more, and utilizing existing structures fully, rather than simply constructing additional volumes. Uniting professional organizations across more than 120 countries, the federation identifies severe housing shortages as a critical challenge for global communities. Architects are urged to combine abstract design capabilities with practical knowledge to establish new governance frameworks, alternative shared ownership models, and environmentally sustainable construction systems. To engage the public and foster broader awareness, the organization encourages architects worldwide to host lectures, exhibitions, and educational outreach initiatives focused on affordability and equitable access.

articles.originalTitle: On World Architecture Day 2026: A Call to Build Better, Build Differently, and Share Resources - archdaily.com
articles.title: International Union of Architects Highlights Global Housing Crisis on World Architecture Day
articles.excerpt: The International Union of Architects marked World Architecture Day by drawing attention to the global housing crisis and equitable access to housing.
articles.content: The International Union of Architects designates the first Monday of October as World Architecture Day, aligning with the United Nations' World Habitat Day. Both occasions drew attention to the global housing crisis as a fundamental element of human dignity and well-being. The union's motto, "Housing is a Human Right. Build It," calls on architects to advance equitable access to housing through design, research, and advocacy. According to United Nations figures, more than 3 billion people lack adequate housing, over 1.1 billion live in informal settlements, and hundreds of millions experience homelessness. The International Union of Architects is a global non-governmental federation uniting professional organizations from more than 120 countries and territories. Recognizing housing shortages as a pressing challenge, the federation emphasizes that housing must not be treated as a luxury asset. On World Architecture Day, the organization invited architects worldwide to promote creative strategies through lectures, exhibitions, and public outreach to address these systemic issues.

articles.originalTitle: Yohji Yamamoto Drawings - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Yohji Yamamoto Drawings Featured at Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.excerpt: Author Alexandre Samson will discuss unpublished drawings by designer Yohji Yamamoto at a special event at the Victoria and Albert Museum.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host author and curator Alexandre Samson alongside Caroline Fabre, executive advisor to Yohji Yamamoto. The event celebrates the publication of Yohji Yamamoto Drawings, featuring previously unpublished sketches selected by Yamamoto himself. Encompassing flaming coats, slumped figures, and elegant dresses, these drawings extend beyond preparatory work to reveal his ongoing exploration of fashion, form, and the body. Supported in design by Peter Saville, the publication unites menswear and womenswear sketches that have remained largely unseen until now. Scheduled for Wednesday from 19.00 to 20.00, the talk will be followed by a wine reception and book signing. Tickets range from 15.00 to 20.00 pounds and include the wine reception. Priority booking is currently available for members and patrons, while general ticket sales will open on 19 October, subject to availability. The event takes place in the Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre at the museum's South Kensington location.

articles.originalTitle: Painting large as an Impressionist: Renoir and the full-length format | Events - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery Examines Renoir and Full-Length Portraiture
articles.excerpt: Colin B. Bailey, Director of The Morgan Library and Museum, will deliver a special lecture at the National Gallery's Pigott Theatre exploring Pierre-Auguste Renoir's large-scale portraits.
articles.content: The National Gallery is hosting a special event focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's full-length portraits, recognized among the most ambitious works of his career. Held in conjunction with the exhibition Renoir and Love, the lecture features Colin B. Bailey, Katharine J. Rayner Director of The Morgan Library & Museum, who will examine how the artist captured modern life, emotions, and social interactions in 19th-century Paris. Drawing on decades of research into eighteenth- and nineteenth-century French art, Bailey will explore Renoir's technical brilliance, evolving portraiture approach, and psychological immediacy. The talk will take place in the Pigott Theatre on Level -1 of the Sainsbury Wing. Standard tickets are priced at 10 pounds, while concessions are available at 8 pounds for full-time students, jobseekers, and disabled adults. Advance booking is required for attendance, and members will have the option to join the event online. This lecture offers audiences a distinct opportunity to closely examine the artist's celebrated figures within the broader context of friendship, love, and modernity explored throughout the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Renoir and Love | Exhibitions - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: National Gallery in London Opens Major Renoir and Love Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition exploring the artist's depiction of human connections and everyday emotions through 40 paintings gathered from international collections, on view until January 31, 2027.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London presents Renoir and Love, an exhibition focusing on Pierre-Auguste Renoir's exploration of love, friendship, and human connection during his peak period from the 1860s to the 1880s. Running until January 31, 2027, the exhibition brings together 40 paintings from collections across the world, highlighting the artist's role as an innovator of Impressionism. Notably, Renoir's iconic 1876 painting Bal au Moulin de la Galette from the Musée d'Orsay is on display in the United Kingdom for the first time. The exhibition is organized jointly by the Musée d'Orsay, the National Gallery, and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Visitors can explore sun-dappled gardens, dance halls, and intimate everyday moments captured by the artist, with flexible pay-what-you-wish admission options available on select Friday evenings.

articles.originalTitle: Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby’s Feed Logic - ArtReview
articles.title: London Exhibition Examines the Evolving Nature of Visual Culture
articles.excerpt: Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby's Bizarre Life exhibition questions the iconographic power of images that lose their photographic identity in the digital age. The show runs until October 3 at Niru Ratnam in London.
articles.content: Artists Laila Majid and Louis Blue Newby explore the logic of the digital feed through drawings, collages, and video works in their exhibition Bizarre Life at Niru Ratnam gallery. The graphite drawings in the Contact series utilize thermal printing software and redrawn lines to present blurred figures, examining the decontextualization of random internet imagery. Wall-mounted assemblages in the Spread series place photographic prints beneath leather-textured silicone skins, juxtaposing everyday objects with unfamiliar elements. The vertical video works, including Inner Heat, bring visual instability into motion through low-resolution, reversed footage of fireworks and a slowed concert recording of Taylor Swift where stage lighting and camera variables abstract the singer's body. Through these distinct visual experiments, the works suggest that images can surrender their photographic identities while retaining a distinct iconographic power. The exhibition remains deliberately unresolved regarding whether this phenomenon serves as a connective or unsettling force for contemporary viewers.

articles.originalTitle: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Roy Lichtenstein Retrospective Opens at Whitney Museum in New York
articles.excerpt: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, marking the artist's first retrospective in New York since 1993 and gathering roughly 130 works created from the early 1940s through the 1990s.
articles.content: The Whitney Museum of American Art in New York hosts Roy Lichtenstein: Like New from October 11, 2026, to May 10, 2027. Marking the artist's first major retrospective in the city since 1993, the exhibition traces how Lichtenstein's early interest in perception and visual recognition shaped a career-long investigation into duplication, simulation, and image culture. Featuring approximately 130 works produced from the early 1940s to the 1990s, the exhibition explores his treatment of images as unstable forms subject to borrowing, translation, and reframing. For the first time, all works from Lichtenstein's inaugural Pop-style exhibition at the Leo Castelli Gallery in 1962 are reunited. This pivotal moment defined an era and extended its impact beyond Pop art, shaping subsequent generations of artists whose works are also displayed within the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - wwd.com
articles.title: Patek Philippe Unveils Its Largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to Date in Milan
articles.excerpt: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe has launched its largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to date at CityOval Milano, featuring over 500 timepieces alongside exclusive limited-edition models created specifically for the Italian market.
articles.content: Swiss luxury watchmaker Patek Philippe has launched the seventh edition of its Watch Art Grand Exhibition at CityOval Milano. Spanning 31,215 square feet, the exhibition showcases over 500 timepieces, including the brand's 1868 wristwatch originally owned by Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Company president Thierry Stern highlighted Italy's long-standing importance as a market of connoisseurs during a preview walk-through. The exhibition is organized across 15 thematic rooms, featuring dedicated spaces for standard-setting calibers, research and development, and complex creations such as the Calibre 89 and Grandmaster Chime. To mark the Milan edition, Patek Philippe debuted seven limited-edition references featuring a sapphire crystal caseback inscribed with Patek Philippe Milano 2026. These include three Calatrava iterations reflecting the Italian flag and world time models with enameled maps of downtown Milan. The exhibition remains open to the public through October 18.

articles.originalTitle: Patek Philippe Unveils Seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan, Debuts Limited-edition Timepieces - WWD
articles.title: Patek Philippe Launches Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan
articles.excerpt: Patek Philippe has launched its largest Watch Art Grand Exhibition to date at CityOval Milano, debuting seven new limited-edition timepieces alongside historical collections.
articles.content: Swiss watchmaker Patek Philippe has opened its seventh Watch Art Grand Exhibition in Milan. Spanning 31,215 square feet at the recently renovated CityOval Milano venue, the exhibition displays over 500 timepieces, including the 1868 wristwatch owned by Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. Company president Thierry Stern noted the longstanding importance of the Italian market and its connoisseurs of rare handcrafts. Running through Oct. 18, the exhibition follows previous editions in cities such as Munich, London, New York, Singapore, Tokyo, and Dubai. To mark the Milan edition, Patek Philippe debuted seven new limited-edition timepieces featuring sapphire crystal casebacks inscribed with 'Patek Philippe Milano 2026.' These include three Calatrava iterations with red, white, and green lacquered dials representing the Italian flag, alongside world time minute repeaters featuring enameled maps of downtown Milan. The brand also introduced the Gondolo Ladies First collection of cushion-shaped jewelry watches featuring gem-set dials and quartz movements. The exhibition coincides with Milano Watch Week at Palazzo Mezzanotte, highlighting the city's growing status as a high-watchmaking hub.

articles.originalTitle: New Work: The Long Goodbye by Carrie Mae Weems - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Carrie Mae Weems Explores Migration and History in New Work at V&A East Museum
articles.excerpt: Commissioned for the opening of V&A East Museum, Carrie Mae Weems's The Long Goodbye explores migration through love stories intertwined within human journeys.
articles.content: Commissioned for the opening of V&A East Museum and developed over nearly three years, The Long Goodbye examines migration through the obscured love stories intertwined within human journeys. The project seeks to restore humanity to individuals whose courage and labor shaped the modern world but whose lives are frequently reduced to statistics or omitted from historical accounts. This commission turns Weems's lens toward the UK and its diasporic communities for the first time. Over the course of its development, Weems's initial ideas evolved in response to migration debates and protests prominent in the political climates of both Britain and the United States. The film imagines a different account of post-war Britain, recognizing the buried truths regarding how and why generations immigrated to the UK. Water functions centrally as a route of migration, a connector between geographies, and a vessel of history. Drawing on the concept of tidalectics developed by Barbadian poet and historian Kamu Brathwaite, the imagery understands history through the ebb and flow of tides. The work is exhibited alongside two archival films, Before the Loss of You and Okwui.

articles.originalTitle: A Metal-Clad Mass-Timber Building by Lever Architecture Unites Portland State University’s Art and Design School - Architectural Record
articles.title: Portland State University art and design school unites in new building
articles.excerpt: Designed by Lever Architecture, the 4-story Jordan Schnitzer building unites three previously dispersed art and design departments at Portland State University under a single roof for the first time.
articles.content: Opening at Portland State University, the four-story, roughly 107,000-square-foot Jordan Schnitzer School of Art + Art History + Design unites three major departments previously dispersed across campus under a single roof. Described by Lever Architecture founding principal Thomas Robinson as cultural infrastructure terminating the city's South Park Blocks, the structure rises from a former parking lot and skate park site. Wrapped in custom-formed green metal panels evoking a forest canopy, the building utilizes cross-laminated timber floor panels and a glulam column-and-beam system, bolstering the region's mass-timber industry. More than half of the Douglas fir glulam used was sourced from tribally owned forests and certified mills across the Pacific Northwest. The building features a central commons area, interconnected exhibition galleries, an open-air courtyard, and studios designed to connect students with the dense urban setting. Brightly colored steel fire stairs and sustainable wood materials complement the architectural design of the facility.

articles.originalTitle: White-brick extension defines Design Museum Gent revamp - Dezeen
articles.title: Design Museum Gent Expands With Waste-Based White Brick Extension
articles.excerpt: Design Museum Gent in Belgium has been revamped and expanded using waste-based white bricks by studios Carmody Groarke, Atama, and Re-st.
articles.content: Design Museum Gent in Belgium has undergone a major revamp led by architecture studios Carmody Groarke, Atama, and Re-st. The project involved restoring three historic wings, renovating an existing courtyard, and adding a timber-framed extension. Spanning a total of 8,600 square metres, the expansion makes the venue Belgium's largest design museum. The extension features a facade of white bricks produced from local construction waste through a low-energy lime-curing process. Developed alongside specialist partners, these bricks are reported to carry one-third of the embodied carbon found in typical Belgian clay bricks. Rising six storeys, the new wing accommodates ground-floor exhibition spaces, lecture and education areas, and a top-level event venue overlooking the city. The building also incorporates a 3D-printed aluminium entrance door by Unfold and works by various local creatives. The museum reopens to the public featuring new collections.

articles.originalTitle: In Oregon, an Elegant Mass-Timber Library by Holst Architecture Makes a Grand Civic Statement - Architectural Record
articles.title: Holst Architecture Completes Mass-Timber East County Library in Gresham, Oregon
articles.excerpt: Designed by Holst Architecture, the 95,000-square-foot East County Library in Gresham, Oregon, opened in May 2026 after a $163 million investment.
articles.content: Located in Gresham, Oregon, the East County Library was designed by Holst Architecture and completed in May 2026. Spanning 95,000 square feet, the project cost $163 million. The facility addresses the shifting demographics and population growth in East Multnomah County over recent decades. The building features a board-formed concrete base supporting massive timber columns and fluted UHPC panels, with a roof extending 55 feet to shelter the entrances. Developed in collaboration with Timberlab, the structure utilizes a Type IV heavy-timber system featuring 96 columns, 1,200 beams, and 300 cross-laminated timber panels left fully exposed. Community outreach played a significant role throughout the design process, resulting in programmatic additions such as a public auditorium, a recording studio, and dedicated rooms for neurodivergent users. Initial design phases involved Adjaye Associates before leadership transitioned to Holst Architecture's Brittany Shreiner. The facility accommodates open stacks for 200,000 books and organizes specific functional spaces around a double-height central atrium illuminated by natural light.

articles.originalTitle: A Warehouse is Converted Into the New Home for Architecture at MIT - Architectural Record
articles.title: MIT Architecture Department Relocates to Historic Converted Warehouse
articles.excerpt: Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro with Leers Weinzapfel, a converted 195,000-square-foot warehouse now houses the MIT Department of Architecture.
articles.content: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology architecture department relocated in August to a 195,000-square-foot converted warehouse located across the street. Designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro in collaboration with Leers Weinzapfel, the conversion project repurposes the five-story brick structure, parts of which date back to 1894, into a new home for architecture, urban studies and planning, and the Morningside Academy for Design. To accommodate these programs within the existing masonry structure featuring low ceilings and a cell-like plan, the design team cut multistory voids within each block and inserted lightweight structural elements to create column-free studio spaces. The conversion incorporates newly cut gridded windows, full-height curtain walls, and concrete shear walls added at the building corners for structural support. Known as the Met Warehouse, the facility also hosts entrepreneurship programs linking the school with surrounding technology and bioscience enterprises.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | India Pavilion: Seeds of the Sacred - A Bharatanatyam Offering to the Human Spirit - labiennale.org
articles.title: India Pavilion Presents Bharatanatyam Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: As part of Biennale Arte 2026, the India Pavilion hosts a traditional Bharatanatyam performance titled Seeds of the Sacred by Anwesha Das.
articles.content: The India Pavilion within the framework of Biennale Arte 2026 presents a special event inviting audiences to explore the strength of the human spirit. Hosted at the Teatro Piccolo Arsenale, the performance titled Seeds of the Sacred - A Bharatanatyam Offering to the Human Spirit is performed by artist Anwesha Das. As one of India's oldest classical dance forms, Bharatanatyam integrates movement, expression, music, and storytelling deeply rooted in tradition. Inspired by the themes of In Minor Keys, this presentation explores authenticity, humility, earth-rootedness, and spiritual proportion. The performance seeks to reconnect audiences with nature and essential human dimensions through bodily movement and gesture. Admission to the event requires a reservation, with the programme scheduled from 19:00 to 20:00.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Step-Free Access Projects Completed at Surrey Quays and Northolt Stations in London
articles.excerpt: Step-free access and infrastructure upgrade projects at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations in London have been completed and opened to the public.
articles.content: Step-free access improvement projects at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations in London have been completed. Surrey Quays station received a new entrance, ticket hall, accessible toilets, footbridge, staircases, and lifts. Funding was provided through the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government Housing Infrastructure Fund alongside contributions from British Land. Lead designer AtkinsRéalis and contractor Morgan Sindall Infrastructure prioritized low carbon impact through the use of low carbon concrete and electric arc furnace steel. Construction utilized a tower crane and electric tools, while engineers designed a specialized piling platform using lightweight foam blocks adjacent to 19th-century retaining walls. Separately, upgrade works at Northolt station introduced a new footbridge and lift to establish step-free access between the street and platforms, marking the 95th station on the network to offer step-free access.

articles.originalTitle: Advancement in Shallow Foundations - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)
articles.title: American Society of Civil Engineers to Host Shallow Foundations Online Session
articles.excerpt: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee is hosting a live stream session covering ground improvement, bearing capacity, and modulus concepts.
articles.content: The Geo-Institute Shallow Foundations Technical Committee within the American Society of Civil Engineers is scheduled to live-stream a technical session covering shallow foundations and ground improvement methodologies. Scheduled for December, the program includes presentations on ground improvement techniques for challenging subsurface conditions, retaining wall designs utilizing lightweight cellular concrete in North Texas, and projected cost savings. The session will also review the fundamental concepts governing the modulus of subgrade reaction, examining the effects of stress and strain levels alongside a comprehensive database of load tests and mat foundations to address scale effects. Additionally, a parametric study will evaluate the stabilization of airfield pavement subgrades on soft soils using recycled plastic pins through finite element analysis. Attendees will examine practical approaches to increasing bearing capacity, reducing settlement, and deploying cost-effective shallow foundation solutions across complex sites.

articles.originalTitle: Chanel Brings Le19M Closer to Chinese Art World, Local Craft With Pudong Art Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Chanel Brings La Galerie Du 19M Exhibition to Pudong Art Museum
articles.excerpt: The Pudong Art Museum in Shanghai hosts its largest exhibition format, bringing together French and Chinese artisans and artists.
articles.content: Seeking to deepen its relationship with Asia, the fashion house opened the latest edition of its project at the Pudong Art Museum on the Huangpu River. Taking over the entire third floor, the free exhibition is its largest format to date and the brand's biggest local project of the year. Following iterations in Dakar and Tokyo, the project brings together ateliers such as Lesage, Montex, Goossens and Lognon alongside more than 31 creative guests from China and France. Arriving amid renewed consumer interest in handicrafts, the exhibition introduces the identity of the brand's Métiers d'Art hub to a local audience. Bruno Pavlovsky stated that the exhibition focuses on the intangible creative process rather than the final products. Curated by Gong Yan, Lin Tianmiao, Zhang Lei and Christelle Kocher, the event highlights sustainability through the upcycling of discarded materials into artworks. Featuring works by artists including Yin Xiuzhen, Ding Yi and Lin Tianmiao, the exhibition will run until November 15.
